errata.error: GESLA 4.1 stamps WSV's hourly means at the start of the hour they average, so every WSV value is labeled 30 minutes before the middle of its hour.
errata.response: The adapter moves every WSV record's times 30 minutes later, to the middle of the hour each value averages.
errata.evidence: At Cuxhaven Steubenhöft in 2015, the value `gesla/cuxhavensteubenhft-5990020-deu-wsv` labels T equals the mean of PEGELONLINE's 1-minute values (`pegelonline/5990020`, in the lake) from T to T + 60 minutes, with a standard deviation of 3.7 mm over 8,757 hours. Against PEGELONLINE's single value at T the spread is 266 mm, and at T + 30 minutes it's 19 mm. BfG's copy of the same gauge (`cuxhaven_steubenhoft-cux-deu-bfg`) matches PEGELONLINE at T exactly, so the offset is in the WSV records only. With the shift, `scripts/clock-check.ts` fits Cuxhaven (against UHSLC's and BfG's TICON records) and Helgoland (against CMEMS's) at 0 minutes. 4.1 fixed 4.0's local time labeled as UTC at WSV; this half hour is what's left.

errata.error: GESLA 4.1 copies UHSLC's Hong Kong (Quarry Bay) records with UHSLC's times, which are an hour early: the height labeled T was measured at T + 1 h UTC.
errata.response: The adapter moves the three records' times an hour later, as the `uhslc` adapter does for UHSLC's own series (erratum `uhslc-hong-kong-hour-early`).
errata.evidence: GESLA's values are UHSLC's at the same labels: on 2010-06-01 at 00:00, 01:00 and 02:00, `hong_kong-329b-hkg-uhslc_rq` gives 2.13, 2.23 and 2.28 m, and UHSLC's ERDDAP (`global_hourly_rqds`, 329 version B) 2130, 2230 and 2280 mm; on 2024-06-01 the fast-delivery record matches `global_hourly_fast` the same way. tide-database found UHSLC's hour against the Hong Kong Observatory's predictions ([openwatersio/slackwater-database#360](https://github.com/openwatersio/slackwater-database/issues/360)). With the shift, `scripts/clock-check.ts` on 2015 fits 329 and 329b at 0 minutes against tide-database's re-fit.

errata.error: Some GESLA 4.1 records change datum partway through while every value stays flagged correct and usable, so a record mixes two zeros meters apart.
errata.response: The adapter checks every coastal record's raw levels for jumps of more than 0.75 m in the 30-day median, and flags each segment that sits more than 0.75 m from the record's longest segment as suspect, keeping GESLA's own flag in `source_flag`. The stations listed are the ones found so far; the check covers any other coastal record.
errata.evidence:
Monthly means of the usable values (QC flag 1, use flag 1):

| Record | Off segment | Main level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cape d'Or, MEDS 240 | 1965-06 to 1965-10: 23.5 to 32.3 m | 5.7 to 6.3 m, 1969 to 1979 |
| Mazatlán float, UNAM 16 | 2021-06-20 to 2021-11-24: −0.1 to 1.5 m | 2.2 to 2.4 m |
| Mazatlán radar, UNAM 16 | to 2021-11-25: 2.8 to 3.4 m | 2.2 to 2.6 m |
| Ōminato, JCG HD04 | 1952: 3.6 to 3.8 m | 1.4 to 1.8 m, 1953 on |
| Gorge at Craigflower, MEDS 7124 | 1969: 2.0 to 2.3 m | 0.8 m, 2011 |

GESLA's metadata marks Cape d'Or and the Mazatlán float record "Possible datum and quality control issues", and Ōminato and Gorge at Craigflower "Possible datum issues", but leaves the values usable. The check found the last two in a random sample of 80 coastal records, and nothing in the other 78.

errata.error: GESLA 4.1's Wewak record (BOM 56070, Papua New Guinea) says its times are UTC+1 (`TIME ZONE HOURS 1`, in the file's header and the metadata CSV), but its values are on UTC. It's the only record in the release that isn't labeled UTC.
errata.response: The adapter keeps Wewak's times as served, on UTC, and ignores the header's time zone. Any other record labeled off UTC is refused rather than converted.
errata.evidence: `scripts/clock-check.ts` on 1990, against UHSLC's TICON record for the same gauge (`wewak-063a-png-uhslc_rq`): as served, the series fits best at −10 minutes (r 0.962) and K1 at −5 minutes. Moved by the header's hour to UTC, it fits best at −70 minutes. UTC+1 isn't Papua New Guinea's time zone either (UTC+10).

errata.error: GESLA 4.1's copies of UHSLC series keep positions UHSLC had when GESLA copied them. UHSLC has corrected most of them since, and 23 records sit 5 to 112 km from their gauge, some at sea or inland.
errata.response: The station refresh moves each record to the gauge's position, listed with its source in `POSITIONS` in `src/positions.ts`. An entry applies only while GESLA still serves the position it was written against; a release that moves the record keeps GESLA's position, and the refresh reports the entry and fails the run until a maintainer checks it. With the positions corrected, eleven GESLA records whose UHSLC links were dropped as 10 to 91 km apart link to UHSLC's series again.

errata.error: GESLA 4.1's Uddevalla record (`uddevalla-2541-swe-smhi`) holds Arkö's data. Its rows are identical to `arko-2545-swe-smhi`, from a Baltic gauge 300 km east, so it has no Skagerrak tide and carries Arkö's mean level. TICON-4's Uddevalla record, fitted from it, has the same error.
errata.response: The record is left out of GESLA's list. SMHI's own series (`smhi/2541`) and GESLA's CMEMS copy (`gesla/uddevalla-udd-swe-cmems`) carry Uddevalla.
errata.evidence: The data rows of the two files from GESLA's CloudFront links are byte-identical, and both match the lake's `smhi/2545` (Arkö) to 0 mm on all 98,855 shared hours. Against SMHI's own Uddevalla series they correlate at r 0.19 to 0.36 hourly. SMHI's Uddevalla matches GESLA's CMEMS copy to 0 mm and nearby Stenungsund at r 0.98. The record starts at Arkö's first hour (2014-04-02), not Uddevalla's (2010-12-15). TICON-4's two records have identical constants (M2 0.008 m) and MSL (0.108 m), while TICON-4's CMEMS Uddevalla has M2 0.141 m. Of GESLA's 71 SMHI records, this is the only one whose start disagrees with SMHI's station of the same ID.

errata.error: From March 2025, GESLA 4.1's St. Pauli record (from CMEMS) has about 16% of its 10-minute values taken from a different minute than its timestamp says. Most are 1 or 2 cm off, but some are up to 42 cm off at mid-tide. GESLA flags all of them as correct and usable.
errata.response: The lake keeps the values as GESLA serves them. The group's preferred station is `pegelonline/5952050`, which takes its history from HPA's own archive on kuestendaten.de, and that archive has the right values.
errata.evidence:
I compared GESLA's record (`stpaulitg-stp-deu-cmems`, created 2026-07-19) with HPA's 1-minute file for gauge 5952050 from kuestendaten.de (downloaded 2026-11-09, shifted from UTC+1 to UTC).

- From 1999-11-01 to 2025-02-28, every one of about 1.3 million shared 10-minute times differs by exactly 5.004 m, which is the gauge zero's offset to NHN. That holds for all 12,954 times in December 2024 to February 2025 too.
- From 2025-03-01 03:40 to the end of the record on 2026-05-31, 12,838 of 65,622 shared times differ. Of those, 10,207 are off by 1 cm, 1,991 by 2 cm, 640 by 3 to 9 cm and 101 by more than 5 cm, up to 42 cm. Every month from March 2025 to May 2026 has between 759 and 931.
- At 11,803 of the 12,838, GESLA's value equals HPA's value from a minute within 10 minutes of the stated time, most often 1 minute before or after. The large differences come from minutes 5 to 29 away, on the steep part of the tide. 5,495 are single points with both 10-minute neighbors matching HPA exactly.
- HPA's series is smooth around these times. Its largest 1-minute step near the 101 large differences is 3 cm. Against Seemannshöft and Blankenese, two HPA gauges downstream, HPA's St. Pauli value is the one that fits the local difference between the gauges at 100 of the 101 large differences. The median departure is 1 cm for HPA and 6 cm for GESLA.
- Example (UTC, meters above gauge zero): on 2025-05-14 06:10, HPA has 6.12 and GESLA 5.82. Seemannshöft has 6.04, and both copies have 6.29 at 06:00 and 5.98 at 06:20.

There's no third copy to compare with. PEGELONLINE's REST API keeps 31 days, and BSH's `508P` holds predictions only.

errata.error: GESLA's copies of UHSLC's Göteborg-Torshamnen (fast delivery and research quality) are stamped one hour early from 23 July to 31 December 2007, as UHSLC's own files are.
errata.response: 23 July to 31 December 2007 is flagged `suspect` in both records, keeping GESLA's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Both records equal `uhslc/819` on every day of 2007, which is an hour early against SMHI's record of the gauge over that span (erratum `uhslc-goteborg-2007-hour-early`). GESLA rates the records usable.

errata.evidence: Both records equal `uhslc/819` on every day of 2011, which is an hour early against SMHI's record of the gauge over that span (erratum `uhslc-goteborg-2011-hour-early`).

errata.evidence: The record equals `uhslc/825` over the span, which differs from PEGELONLINE's and GESLA's other Cuxhaven records by 56 cm RMS (erratum `uhslc-cuxhaven-2024-march`).

errata.error: GESLA's CMEMS record of Büsum has spikes of up to 3 m and repeated values from February 2024 to early May 2025 that PEGELONLINE's record of the gauge doesn't have.
errata.response: 25 February 2024 to 4 May 2025 is flagged `suspect`, keeping GESLA's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Found by the cross-station checks in `scripts/cross-check.ts` ([#121](https://github.com/openwatersio/water-levels/pull/121)), November 2026. The record equals PEGELONLINE's Büsum (`pegelonline/9510095`) to 0.0 cm through January 2024. From 25 February 2024 it differs by 3 cm RMS on most days, from values held for several 10-minute steps, and by 34 to 101 cm on 25 February, 18 March, 22 April and 1 to 3 August 2024, from spikes of up to 3 m. From 5 May 2025 to the record's end in May 2026 it matches PEGELONLINE's again, within 2 cm RMS every day.

errata.error: GESLA's records of six USGS tide gauges in New Jersey run an hour late from 6 April to 9 May 2003, starting the day daylight saving time began.
errata.response: 6 April to 9 May 2003 is flagged `suspect` at the six gauges, keeping GESLA's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Found by the cross-station checks in `scripts/cross-check.ts` ([#121](https://github.com/openwatersio/water-levels/pull/121)), November 2026: the tide-timing check put all six 49 to 71 minutes late in the windows from 8 April to 8 May 2003, and nowhere near that before or after. Day by day, Cape May Harbor's tide best matches CO-OPS's Atlantic City (`coops/8534720`) at a 60-minute lag before 6 April and after 9 May, and at 120 minutes between. The lake's own USGS series of these gauges start later, so only GESLA's records hold the span.

errata.error: GESLA's RWS record of Eemshaven Waddenzee sits 15 to 20 cm higher than usual against Delfzijl from 7 April to 11 May 2016.
errata.response: 7 April to 11 May 2016 is flagged `suspect`, keeping GESLA's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Found by the cross-station checks in `scripts/cross-check.ts` ([#121](https://github.com/openwatersio/water-levels/pull/121)), November 2026: a step of +18 cm against three of three neighboring gauges on 8 April 2016 and back on 20 May. Daily means against GESLA's Delfzijl (`gesla/delfzijl-del-nld-rws`) are about −9 cm through March and from mid-May, +1 cm on 7 April, and +7 to +12 cm on most days from 14 April to 11 May, falling to −3 cm on 12 May. The step check compares 30-day medians, so its dates are a few days off; the span follows the daily means.

errata.evidence: GESLA's WSV record of the gauge, hourly means of the values PEGELONLINE serves, equals PEGELONLINE's over the span: daily means differ by 0.0 cm at the median, 0.2 cm standard deviation, over 305 days (erratum `pegelonline-helgoland-binnenhafen-2000-offset`).

errata.error: GESLA's SMHI record of Göteborg-Eriksberg holds Tingstadstunneln's levels from 1 January to 12 November 2018, as SMHI's own does.
errata.response: 1 January to 12 November 2018 is flagged `suspect`, keeping GESLA's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Its daily means equal SMHI's Eriksberg (`smhi/33096`) to 0.0 cm at the median over 297 days of the span (erratum `smhi-eriksberg-2018-tingstadstunneln`). GESLA's CMEMS record of the gauge differs from SMHI's by 5 cm at the median over the span, and agrees outside it, so it may hold Eriksberg's own levels.
